description: ČNB publishes only national aggregates for cards, ATMs and POS terminals; no issuer-, acquirer- or scheme-level breakdown and no merchant-category detail.

Payment statistics are quarterly/semi-annual with a substantial publication lag, whereas CERTIS volumes are monthly. Card and terminal counts therefore update far more slowly than transaction volumes.

Payment statistics were re-based in 2022 following ECB Reg. (EU) 2020/2011 and CZ Decree 401/2021 Sb., with new report codes and a new coding scheme for payments. Pre-2022 and post-2022 series are not automatically comparable.
ARAD is a JavaScript SPA with hash routing; the underlying REST API surface, indicator identifiers and rate limits have not been enumerated in this pass.

The English mirror of cnb.cz was confirmed to exist for the main statistics, CERTIS and payments pages, but English mirrors were not located for the deeper methodology and reporting pages (vykazování, metodické poznámky) or for the cnBlog cash posts.
Cash-usage evidence from ČNB is supply-side (currency in circulation, denominations, counterfeits). ČNB payment-diary or consumer cash-behaviour survey material was not located in this pass.
Exact ECB Data Portal series keys for Czechia POS terminals, ATMs, card counts and card transaction values were not enumerated in this pass — only the dataset and category level was established.

The break between the pre-2022 ECB PSS regime and the post-2022 PAY regime under Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 is known to exist but its concrete effect on CZ terminal and card series has not been characterised.

Non-ECB European supranational layers were not exhausted: OECD statistics, the European Commission/DG FISMA PSD2 review evidence base, ESRB, and EU open-data portal (data.europa.eu) mirrors of payments data were not searched in this pass.

No supranational source found that measures CZ cash usage at point of sale in a harmonised, behaviour-level way (SPACE excludes CZ; BIS excludes CZ; Findex measures account/digital-payment use rather than POS payment shares).

Only two Czech-language queries were run within this cell and both resolved to national rather than supranational material; Czech terminology for supranational dataset concepts (e.g. akceptační místa, platební terminály, harmonizovaná statistika) remains only partially mapped.
Redistribution and licensing terms were inferred rather than read for IMF FAS, BIS and Findex microdata.
Cash-in-transit actor map is incomplete: only Loomis, Brink's and G4S were confirmed. Smaller regional processors licensed under Act 136/2011 are not yet enumerated.
No municipality-level dataset of ATM/branch presence was located; evidence is anecdotal (individual town closures) or aggregated nationally.
Czech Banking Association (Česká bankovní asociace, ČBA) was not directly searched in this pass despite being the most likely publisher of branch/cash-desk aggregates and cash-usage surveys.
No EU-level comparator source was captured (ECB SPACE-type cash-usage studies, ESTA CIT industry data, EPC cash reports) to benchmark CZ against euro-area cash trends.
No paid/commercial dataset vendors (RBR/Datos ATM benchmarking, Euromonitor, ATM Marketplace intelligence) were assessed for CZ ATM-estate coverage.

Bank-owned and international acquirers serving Czech merchants (Global Payments CZ / KB SmartPay, Worldline, Nexi, ČSOB, Komerční banka, Air Bank's 'Cvak' A2A scheme, Adyen CZ) were not individually scouted in this pass, although Comgate's disclosures show Cvak is already material.

Large individual merchants that disclose payment-mix or basket statistics (Alza, Rohlik, Mall/Allegro CZ, Notino, Dr.Max) were not covered; their annual reports and PR can carry acceptance-side datapoints.

Official statistical and regulatory anchors for the acceptance side (ČSÚ e-commerce/retail statistics, ČNB payment-system statistics, Eurostat ICT usage) were deliberately out of this cell but are needed to normalise the commercial claims collected here.
Most acceptance-side quantitative claims found are point-in-time PR statements without back-series; only Heureka's quarterly Insider offers a genuinely repeating time series.
Access and licensing terms were not verified for the two most valuable structured portals (data.apek.cz and ceska-ecommerce.cz), nor were their underlying data endpoints inspected.

Czech-domiciled boutique financial analysts and consultancies covering payments (e.g. local fintech advisory shops, bank-owned analytical teams beyond Raiffeisen and Erste, and the analytical units of KB/ČSOB/ČS) were not systematically enumerated in this slice.

Analyst coverage specifically of ATM networks and cash-in-transit economics in CZ was not found in this cell — the found aggregator reports address POS terminals, cards and e-commerce, but not ATM estate sizing or cash-cycle cost analysis.

Paid-report distributor and abstract aggregators beyond the ones found (e.g. ReportLinker, MarketResearch.com, EMIS/ISI Emerging Markets, Euromonitor Passport, GlobalData's own portal) were not enumerated, yet they are the standard route to CZ payment market abstracts.
Most consumer-survey evidence found dates to 2022–2024 waves; whether these series continued into 2025–2026 was not established for STEM/MARK, GfK CZ or the Index prosperity payment chapter.

The regional bank-research layer (RBI, Erste) was reached only in English; whether Czech-language versions of the CEE Banking Sector Report or Czech-desk notes exist for local audiences was not tested.

Card-scheme-commissioned research (Mastercard CZ, Visa CZ press studies) appeared repeatedly in the media layer as a source of Czech payment-behaviour statistics but sits at the boundary of this cell and was not catalogued here.
No licensed CZ press-archive/monitoring service is in scope, yet HN/Ekonom/E15 full text is where fleet and share figures actually appear.
Slovak-language and cross-border CZ/SK trade press was not covered in this cell, though CZ-SK vendor deals are often reported only on the Slovak side.
Only text web media were scouted; CZ banking/payments podcasts, conference recordings and video interviews were not enumerated.
No URL in this slice was confirmed reachable by fetch; all entries rest on search-result evidence only.
Most press figures trace back to two primaries (SBK — Sdružení pro bankovní karty, and ČNB payment statistics) not owned by this cell.

Career portals were confirmed for KB, ČSOB, Global Payments Europe, Worldline and Nexi, but not yet for Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, Air Bank/Moneta, UniCredit CZ, Fio, Partners Banka, or for local terminal/processor players (Sonet, Monet+, Twisto/Zonky-type fintechs).
Only fragments of historic conference agendas were located (cardforum 2022 PDF, cardforum 2024 write-up). No systematic multi-year agenda archive was found for any Czech payments event.

Non-LinkedIn social/community weak-signal channels were not explored: X/Twitter accounts (e.g. @Card_Forum surfaced but was not assessed), Czech fintech podcasts, YouTube recordings of conference sessions, and Slack/Discord-style practitioner communities.

Cash usage and ATM estate signals are thin in this cell: no cash-handling/ATM-operator conference, award or hiring channel was identified (e.g. Euronet CZ, cash-in-transit operators, ČNB cash-cycle events).

No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; all reachability assessments are inferences from search-result metadata. Several legacy SBK domains and retired event pages are plausible 404/moved candidates.
No mechanism identified yet that proactively captures ČNB/ČSÚ payment-statistics pages at the moment of publication, so restructuring risk is only partly mitigated by opportunistic Wayback crawls.

The cell established the registry infrastructure (ARES, dataor, or.justice.cz) but did not yet enumerate the specific CZ payment-sector legal entities (acquirers, ATM independent deployers, cash-in-transit, POS vendors, payment institutions) whose filings should be tracked.
The English-language re-publication layer is dominated by one consumer outlet (Expats.cz); ČTK's English wire — the likely main channel — is subscription-gated and was not accessed.
Newsletter-format aggregators (Czech fintech/banking newsletters, LinkedIn-native digests) were not covered; only RSS-based aggregation was mapped.
robots.txt, rate limits and terms of use were not inspected for or.justice.cz, dataor.justice.cz, ares.gov.cz or web.archive.org in this run.
Point-of-sale tender mix (cash vs card vs mobile wallet) is not covered by any national statistical or ministry source identified in this cell.

Digitální a informační agentura (DIA), the operator of data.gov.cz and gov.cz service catalogue, was not directly profiled; nor were subordinate MF bodies (Celní správa, Generální finanční ředitelství) as individual open-data publishers.
Microdata access routes were not investigated: ČSÚ anonymised microdata (SRÚ, SILC, ICT surveys) are available only under a formal request/contract procedure that was not documented in this pass.
English coverage of this cell is thin: only 'Information Society in Figures' and the MPO portal English mirror were confirmed. Most ministry and open-data material is Czech-only.
Release calendars were not captured. ČSÚ 'Rychlé informace' publish on a fixed schedule and MF reports annually mid-year, but exact dates were not collected.

No association was found representing merchant acquirers or payment-terminal operators as a distinct group, and none representing independent ATM deployers. SBK's observer list is the closest proxy but its composition was not directly verified in this pass (the mirror host failed TLS).

SBK claims card statistics from 2000 to 2026 plus a historical Excel from 1989, but the exact download URL pattern under /statistiky/download/ was inferred from relative paths rather than confirmed file-by-file.

English-language association output is thin: only czech-ba.cz/en, apek.cz/en and ČLFA's English-titled quarterly results page were found. SBK, AKAT, APNÚ, AČSS and the fintech association publish substantively in Czech only.

APEK's annual E-commerce Study — the richest association source on e-commerce payment mix and cash-on-delivery decline — is free to members and presumably paid otherwise. Only press-release-level figures are openly available. APNÚ's new credit register is likewise presumably members-only.

Several adjacent CZ bodies were not searched in this pass for time reasons: Česká asociace pojišťoven (insurance, for bancassurance/insurtech overlap), Asociace družstevních záložen / kampeliček (credit unions), any CZ crypto-asset industry association (relevant post-MiCA for payments), and Hospodářská komora ČR sectoral sections.
AČSS explicitly states its statistics derive from the Ministry of Finance, and several association aggregates may similarly re-publish ČNB or ministry data with association framing.

Scheme press releases are the only source of CZ volume/penetration figures, and older releases are periodically pruned from scheme CMSs (2015-2019 Visa Europe CZ contactless figures now survive mainly in third-party media).

Scheme CZ figures are routinely attributed to Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK/SDKB, the Czech Bank Card Association) rather than produced independently by the scheme — the association is the upstream aggregator for much of what Visa/Mastercard quote locally.
Scheme-fee and cost-of-acceptance evidence for CZ rests on a single acquirer document (Worldline). No comparison set exists yet.

Cash usage and ATM economics are barely covered by scheme sources — schemes publish card/contactless penetration but say little about CZ cash withdrawal volumes, and ATM interchange appears only as a line item inside the interchange PDFs.
The mandatory-disclosure layer (interchange, rulebooks) is English-only while the statistical layer (press releases) is strongest in Czech — neither language alone covers the cell.
Smaller international networks in CZ (JCB, Discover/PULSE post-Diners, and any emerging account-to-account scheme positioning against cards) are undocumented in this pass.
Cash usage and ATM estate operators (independent ATM deployers, cash-in-transit, Euronet-style networks in CZ) were not covered in this cell's pass.
Company financial filings (Sbírka listin / justice.cz) for processors and acquirers were identified as a method but not enumerated as concrete sources.
CERTIS/instant-payments technical scheme documentation (ISO 20022 message specs, scheme rulebook annexes) was not individually catalogued beyond the rules landing page.
English-language CZ-specific sources are thin: most rail and standards documentation exists only in Czech; the EPC/ECB sources are the main en-language anchors.
Card transaction values/volumes (as opposed to card counts) are not disclosed per-bank; only issuance counts and network sizes appear.

Smaller but payment-relevant CZ banks outside the named eight (Česká spořitelna's Erste ecosystem partners, Trinity Bank, Creditas, Max banka, Partners Banka, plus Revolut/N26 branch presence) were not covered in this cell.
Most actor-level metrics are locked in narrative PDF/XHTML annual reports rather than machine-readable series; ESEF XHTML covers only tagged financials, not card/ATM counts.
Unlisted banks (Air Bank, Fio, Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit CZ) report operational metrics only annually with a 4-month lag, while listed KB/MONETA and parents Erste/KBC report quarterly.

Cash-in-transit and cash-cycle service providers serving CZ ATM fleets (e.g. Loomis, G4S/Brink's-type operators) were not searched in this pass, although they are a distinct vendor tier revealing cash-usage volumes and ATM servicing economics.

Company-register and financial-filing sources (ARES, justice.cz Sbirka listin) were identified as a triangulation route but not actually collected. Vendor CZ subsidiaries file accounts that quantify revenue and headcount - a hard check on marketing claims.

Vendor job postings, partner/certification directories and conference/exhibitor lists (e.g. CZ banking IT conferences, ATMIA/Money20/20 exhibitor rosters) were not exploited. These indirectly reveal platform stacks and account teams per CZ bank.

Global vendor sites (Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, KAL, Nexi) publish CZ-relevant material almost exclusively in English; no Czech-language mirrors of these case studies were located, so Czech-only monitoring would miss the highest-value fleet statistics.

Several fleet and estate figures encountered (CSOB ~1,025 self-service devices, Ceska sporitelna 1,600+ ATMs, Euronet ~600-700 ATMs, Air Bank ~160 terminals in 2017) come from single vendor or media sources with differing vintages and no consistent definition of what counts as a device.

Municipal and regional buyers (cities, kraje, municipal transport companies outside Prague and Olomouc, parking operators, waterworks, hospitals) were only sampled, not enumerated. Each runs its own profile, so the long tail of POS/CIT tenders is unmapped.
No CPV code list was fixed for this domain in this pass; keyword-only search will under-recall tenders titled generically (e.g. 'bezpečnostní služby' covering CIT).
Confirmed examples cluster in 2017-2021; no 2024-2026 payment/cash tender was verified in this pass, so current incumbents and current volumes are not evidenced.
Legal/re-use terms of the commercial aggregators (Tender Arena, vhodne-uverejneni, openprocurements, najdivz) and of the Hlídač státu API were not reviewed.
Administrative court judgment databases (nssoud.cz for the Supreme Administrative Court, and the Krajský soud v Brně as the first-instance reviewer of ÚOHS decisions) were not searched.

Passporting/notification records — EEA payment institutions and credit institutions notifying cross-border provision into CZ, and CZ entities notifying outward — were not individually located, though they are known to sit inside JERRS and the EBA registers.

Other CZ authorities with adjacent supervisory outputs were not covered: Česká obchodní inspekce (ČOI) for merchant-side conduct and surcharging, Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů (ÚOOÚ) for payment-data cases, and the Finanční analytický úřad (FAÚ) for AML measures against payment institutions.
The ČNB became supervisor for the crypto-asset sector under MiCA (noted in the 2025 supervision report), implying a new CZ register of crypto-asset service providers that was not located in this run.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable; all were derived from search-result evidence. JERRS in particular uses generated, session-bound URLs.
